title: The 3.8.0 med defects are fixed: locks, guard false positive, the affected listing, dependants at mint, and the empty task gate
description: D9: a med defect holds a release. Register entries F754, F800, F809 (open part), F792 (with its P151 recurrences) and F779, each verified open against main on 2026-10-29/31, plus F821's release-tier flake in tests/test__locks.py.
desiredOutcome: Each entry's Do is met with a case that goes red on the defect, the register status of each reads FIXED with its commit, and release-tier CI is green on the phase's landing commit.

findings.issue: The new predicate keys on the stored basis (`_mio.gate_cleared(tests)`, i.e. gateBasis == `cleared`) rather than on the gate that actually measures the task. Its own docstring says 'the phase's own gate may be empty too', and in that state the defect the task describes ('A task can close with no gate while the record reads green') is still open by a second shape: a tdd/regression task whose own tests.gate is absent or [] with no basis falls back to its phase (`_manifest_io.gate_entries`, _manifest_io.py:685-692), an empty phase testGate is a designed, validator-accepted state (`_manifest_phases.py:791`, `phase add --gate-clear`), `run-test-gate` answers `empty-gate` with exit 0 (run-test-gate.py:5401-5420), and `done` closes it via `_close_gate`'s arm '%s declares no gate, nor does its phase, so its close rests on its commit alone' (audit-task.py:7289-7313) - `_owed_case_gate_refusal` returns None because gateBasis is not `cleared`. Judged by reading, not run.
findings.resolution: Ask the refusal at `done` (and, if wanted, at the writes) of the resolved gate: refuse when tests.mode is tdd/regression and `_mio.gate_entries(phase, node)[0]` is empty, which covers both the cleared gate and the fallback to an empty phase gate; add a case beside ocg8 with a tdd task carrying no own gate in a phase whose testGate is [] (and its gate-only second-direction pair).

findings.issue: On a STARTED task the scope refusal prints `_OWED_CASE_WRITE_REMEDY`, whose second half ('--tests-mode gate-only if it owes no case of its own') is itself refused: a tests.mode change on a started task is a narrowing `_narrowings` blocks (fg6 pins 'already been attempted'), unlike tests.gate which is `_FORWARD_ONLY`. The `done` arm already words its remedy for this ('A started task may still move its gate ... so the remedy is the gate and not the mode'); the scope arm does not, so e.g. `scope <started tdd task> --gate-clear` names a dead-end remedy.
findings.resolution: Pass `_started(node)`-dependent remedy text at the _locked_scope call site (the gate-only half only for a task not yet started), and pin it with a case on a started tdd task asserting '--tests-mode gate-only' is absent from the refusal.

findings.issue: User-visible behaviour changed and the surfaces describing `--gate-clear` still say it is how a task reaches the EMPTY gate ('`--gate-clear` for none'), with no mention that a tdd/regression task (including one whose mode `add` derived from its title) is now refused and must pass `--tests-mode gate-only`. The executor named this follow-up itself; it is outside the task's declared files.
findings.resolution: Add one sentence to each surface (or to verbs-in-full.md and point the others at it) stating the refusal and its two remedies, and a CHANGELOG entry for the new refusal.

findings.issue: done refuses a tdd/regression task only on a stored cleared gateBasis; a task with no gate of its own whose phase gate is empty still closes green through the declares-no-gate branch of _close_gate
findings.resolution: refuse when the gate that would actually run (_mio.gate_entries(phase, node)) is empty for a tdd/regression task; fix the scope refusal hint on a started task (mode change is refused there); document the refusal in commands/task.md, reference/verbs-in-full.md, README and CHANGELOG

tasks.title: A phase lock held by the caller's own process under an earlier session id is reported as the caller's, and a dead drive's lock is not read as a live run
tasks.description: Register F754. When a Claude Code conversation continues under a new session id in the same process, the phase lock taken under the old id reads as HELD by a live run forever (the holder pid is the long-lived claude process), and only release --session <old> --pid <pid> lets go. Do: when the caller's process ancestry contains the holder pid but the session differs, say so and offer the release by name; and base liveness on the drive command's own pid or a heartbeat rather than the long-lived claude process, so a dead drive releases. A lock held by an unrelated live pid still refuses.

add: tests/test__locks.py: a lock held by an ancestor pid under another session id is reported as the caller's own with the release offered by name; a lock held by an unrelated live pid still refuses

outcome.technical:

--session --pid `, shlex-quoted, shlex imported lazily since hooks resolve this module on every tool call). acquire's E_LIVE refusal and release's mismatch refusal both use it: the exit code stays E_LIVE and the claim is never adopted, only named and offered. Module docstring gains one paragraph; PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md's _locks section gains the matching sentence. tests/test__locks.py: new ap-block (_ancestor_cases) with ap1, ap1b, ap1c, ap1d, ap1e, ap2, ap2b, ap2c, ap3; wt3 not touched. tasks.title: guard-uncommitted reads a heredoc body or a quoted argument as data, not as a command, so a description that quotes git is not refused
tasks.description: Register F800. The guard refused an audit-task.py add whose heredoc description merely quoted git commands: it could not tokenize the command, assumed the widest loss set, and refused; the same description passed on stdin from a file. Bind the evidence to the operation: when the command cannot be tokenized, read only what is outside heredoc bodies and quoted arguments; red-first the allow case and keep the deny case red.

add: .claude/hooks/guard-uncommitted.py: an audit-task add whose heredoc description quotes a stash command and a checkout is allowed; the same commands run outside the heredoc are still refused

outcome.technical: guard-uncommitted.py: when the sibling parser cannot tokenize a line, reading() now builds executed_text(command), a quote- and heredoc-aware walk. It drops quoted-delimiter heredoc bodies, including one inside a command substitution inside double quotes (the house description form), and drops quoted ARGUMENTS. It keeps every command substitution and backquote, inside double quotes and inside unquoted-delimiter bodies too. It keeps a quoted program word and every quoted argument of git. It truncates at a quote or substitution that never closes; bash runs nothing past one, verified with bash -c on an unterminated quote, which ran only the earlier complete lines. It returns None, keeping the raw-line reading and the unchanged widest refusal, when any command in the line can run text it is handed: a shell, eval, make, xargs or exec, a program named by path, or an interpreter not running a script file. That judgement uses the shared _config.program_candidates, is_shell, is_interpreter and runs_own_program. The view is re-parsed with the sibling's git_invocations and judged on the operation; that reading is labelled 'executed', and its refusal says the line could not be tokenized and what was read. If the view will not parse either, the shapes grade the view. Also fixed: the pre-filter's tree-wide dot (_DOT) now ends where a shell word ends, so a variable assigned from a substitution running a tree-wide checkout is no longer waved through before the parser is asked; it was allowed on HEAD, tokenizable or not. gu41 is reworded to assert the 'could not be tokenized' basis: its old 'TEXT' assertion now belongs to the raw path, and gu51 pins the two labels apart. New cases gu43-gu51. Selftest 52/52. Gate `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py .claude/hooks/guard-uncommitted.py` exit 0 (1/1 files ok, 52 cases). Mutation probe: <scratchpad>/p153-3/probe/mutations.py, output in output.txt beside it, run as `python3 mutations.py <checkout>`. Baseline 52/52, and all nine rows were KILLED, including both over-fire directions (M8 every interpreter a runner turned gu44 and gu49 red; M9 every command a runner did the same) and the defect restored (M1 turned gu44 and gu49 red). Probe exit 0. REFUSALS, verbatim apart from paths: (a) the plan gate refused probe/mutations.py inside the worktree: '[require-plan] probe/mutations.py is outside task P153.3, the task this worktree is bound to (plan: <home>/dev/audit-plugin/claude-plugins): no task of this plan declares it for this one. Only that task's files are open here.' The probe therefore lives in the scratchpad. (b) The first submit call was refused by the live plugin guard-history-rewrite, whose message opens: '[guard-history-rewrite] `git st` + `ash` moves work between the working tree and the stash' (spelled split here for the same reason). The return object's prose quoted the stash command, and because the heredoc head names its script by a QUOTED path, _config._plain_script_run does not vouch for it, so the body was graded as code and fell to the raw-text arm. (c) The second submit was refused for absolute machine paths; this filing writes <home>/ and <scratchpad>/. Apart from those spellings, the content is unchanged. CONTRIBUTING.md gains one Hard-rules bullet: a guard grades what a command executes in its fallback too. It names executed_text() and its selftest, and says nothing enforces the rule for a guard added later. Extra checks: ruff on the hook reports only a pre-existing unused shutil import in _selftest (present on HEAD; .claude/hooks is outside CI's ruff scope). vermin 3.8 ok. house_style_violations, prose_number_claims and doc_prose_numbers: 0 findings. Dependant suites tests/test__areas.py, test__deps.py, test__output_lints.py and test_derive_phase_gate.py via the sweep: 4/4 ok, 593 cases. tools/prove-gates.py: no row anchors on this hook (a grep for the hook name in tools/, tests/ and .github/ hits only .github/sweep-costs.json), so no row needs changing. Dependants: .claude/settings.json registers the hook by path, and the contract (stdin payload, deny JSON, exit 0) is unchanged, so it is still correct. .github/sweep-costs.json's figure for this file still matches (the sweep ran in 1.0s). The names targets, judge, parser and decide found in guard-release.py, require-claim-block.py, the skills and CHANGELOG are those files' own same-named symbols: .claude hooks do not import this file, and none of this file's signatures changed, so they are still correct. CONTRIBUTING.md's basename dependants (evals.json, _output.py, the four suites above, tools/affected.py, tools/check-committed-pii.py) reference the file, not this bullet, and no heading was renamed; still correct, and the suites are green. FOUND, OUT OF SCOPE (not edited; not a declared file): the root of the tokenized-path half is _config._head_runs_body in plugins/audit/hooks/_config.py. Its _HEAD_INDIRECTION search matches the command substitution that ENCLOSES the cat heredoc, so every house-form body (commit message or description) is graded as SHELL by every guard sharing split_heredocs. Measured: git_invocations on an audit-task add whose house-form description has a body line opening with the stash verb returns a stash invocation with args ['is','banned','here']. A body line opening with a tree-wide checkout would be refused by this guard on the tokenized path, and the plugin's history guard reads the same bodies as commands; refusal (b) above is a second instance of the class. The fix belongs in _config: read the head from the innermost open substitution, and stop letting a quoted script path disqualify a plain script run. It needs a register entry and its own task.
outcome.descriptive: guard-uncommitted no longer refuses a command for heredoc bodies or quoted arguments that only quote destructive git, while every real destructive command stays refused, including one inside a command substitution that the pre-filter used to miss.

tasks.title: scope --gate-clear on a tdd or regression task refuses, or falls back to the phase gate, rather than closing the task with no gate
tasks.description: Register F779 (verified 2026-10-31 at ad838231): audit-task.py scope <task> --gate-clear on a tdd task exits 0 and writes {gate: [], gateBasis: cleared}; run-test-gate reports empty-gate. A task can close with no gate while the record reads green. Pick the structurally correct answer (refuse on tdd/regression, or fall back to the phase gate with the basis saying so) and check the drive's close path end to end.

add: tests/test_audit_task.py: scope --gate-clear on a tdd task neither writes an empty gate silently nor lets the task close as green

outcome.technical: DESIGN: refuse, not fall back. A tdd/regression task whose tests.gateBasis is `cleared` is now refused wherever a write would leave that state, and `done` refuses to close one. I chose refusal over falling back to the phase gate for three reasons. (1) The fallback answers a request for no gate with a gate nobody named, usually the phase's widest one. (2) The phase gate may itself be empty (P3 in the fixture), so a fallback does not close the state. (3) mode and gate contradict each other and only the caller knows which is wrong, so the refusal names both remedies (`--gate <cmd>` / `--tests-mode gate-only`). An empty task gate with NO basis already falls back to the phase (_manifest_io.gate_entries, _manifest_io.py:689), so the defect state is exactly mode in {tdd, regression} AND gate_cleared(tests). CODE (plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/audit-task.py): new `_OWES_CASE_MODES` (derived from _vocab.TESTS_MODE minus gate-only), `_owed_case_gate_refusal(tid, tests, remedy)` and `_OWED_CASE_WRITE_REMEDY`, placed beside `_retarget_gate_contradiction`. Called from (a) _locked_scope after the widening guard and before any write, judged on the tests block the call leaves, only when the call writes tests; (b) _locked_add, beside _files_gate_refusal; (c) the add --from-file batch loop, beside _files_gate_refusal; (d) _locked_done, right after the not-started refusal and before both close arms (--commit and --no-change). The scope check sits AFTER the started-task widening guard so a started task's mode change still meets the mode refusal first (fg6). The dispatch path is untouched (P153.6). CLOSE PATH TRACED: drive-phase.py close_task (line ~3905) commits via commit-task-work.py or writer_commit and then always runs `audit-task.py done <id> --commit <sha> --from-return`; the no-change exit (drive-phase.py ~6484) runs `done --no-change`. With a cleared gate, run-test-gate.py (~5401) answers empty-gate and exits 0, and commit-task-work.py (docstring 116-121, line 763) commits 'bound to no verdict'. So `done` was the one door, and on HEAD it closed such a task done (ocg8 and ocg9 were red on HEAD with code 0 and status done). Every drive close now goes through the _locked_done refusal. TESTS (tests/test_audit_task.py): a new block `_tdd_gate_clear_cases`, stage `ocg-block`, appended to STAGES. Cases ocg1/ocg1b/ocg2/ocg2b cover scope --gate-clear on tdd/regression: refused, no byte written, both remedies named. ocg3 is the second direction (--tests-mode gate-only --gate-clear allowed). ocg4 covers --tests-mode tdd over a cleared gate. ocg5 pins the existing refusal of a gate-drop of the last entry, which already passed on HEAD. ocg6 is the second direction (a drop that leaves an entry still lands). ocg7 covers add --tests-mode tdd --gate-clear: refused, no id minted. ocg12 covers an add --from-file batch whose tdd task has gate []. ocg8 covers done on a started tdd task with a cleared gate: refused, remedy `scope P2.4 --gate`. ocg11 checks that remedy lands on the started task. ocg9 covers done --no-change on a regression task. ocg10 is the second direction (a gate-only cleared task still closes). EXISTING CASES ADJUSTED, all in my own file, and each was a fixture whose tdd mode was incidental to its point: ag1 now passes --tests-mode gate-only (the title derives tdd; ag2-ag4 and ag8 had cascaded from it). at5-block tg9 now passes --tests-mode gate-only (gb1 had cascaded). The fg fixture's running task is gate-only rather than tdd, because fg4/fg5 clear its gate; fg6's expected text now reads from "gate-only" to "regression". The add --from-file remedy-following case applies the gate_clear edit to tasks[1] (gate-only) rather than tasks[0] (tdd). RUNS: red on HEAD code before the fix, `python3 tests/test_audit_task.py --selftest --stage tg-block` (the block's name before the rename): exit 1, 4/12 cases passed. The failures were tg1, tg1b, tg2, tg2b, tg4, tg7, tg8 and tg9, i.e. ocg1-ocg9 less ocg3/ocg5/ocg6 under today's names; ocg11 and ocg12 were added after the fix and are proven by the mutation rows below. The first full-gate run failed on 23 DUPLICATE CASE ID errors (the `tg` prefix already lives in at5-block) plus the cascades listed above; I renamed my ids to `ocg`. Final gate: `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_audit_task.py` exit 0, '1/1 files ok, 1180 cases'. MUTATION PROBE: the plan gate refused writing probe/mutations.py in the worktree, verbatim: "[require-plan] probe/mutations.py is outside task P153.4, the task this worktree is bound to (plan: <home>/dev/audit-plugin/claude-plugins): no task of this plan declares it for this one. Only that task's files are open here." It therefore lives at <scratchpad>/P153.4-probe/mutations.py. Run it as `python3 mutations.py <tree>`; it mutates a copy of the tree, never the tree itself. Its output is in mutations.out.txt beside it: baseline 14/14; all 7 rows KILLED; restored 14/14; exit 0. The rows: scope check off -> ocg1,1b,2,2b,4 red; add check off -> ocg7; batch check off -> ocg12; done check off -> ocg8,9; mode ignored (over-fire) -> ocg3,10; basis ignored (over-fire) -> ocg6,11; gate-only counted as owing a case -> ocg3,10. A sibling agent sharing this session's scratchpad overwrote my first copy at scratchpad/probe/mutations.py, which is why it moved to the task-unique directory. PROVE-GATES: `python3 tools/prove-gates.py --list | grep -i audit-task` gives no row anchored in audit-task.py. The only removed lines in my diff are the two `_files_gate_refusal(task, phase, assembled)` call lines, and no tools/ file references them (grep). DEPENDANTS: test__output.py, tools/affected.py, PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md, docs/research/*.md and hooks/journal-writes.py reference audit-task.py by path or basename. Nothing was renamed or moved, so they are still correct. The names used elsewhere (_allocate_phase_id, _cancel_task, _create_then, _done_details) are unchanged. tests/test_commit_task_work.py imports _attempt_cases, _close_evidence_cases and _remedies_pass, and tests/test__filed_returns.py imports _held_cases; all are unchanged, so still correct. .github/sweep-costs.json has no figure for the new ocg-block, and the sweep weighs it by the suite's figure over its blocks; a re-record would add it. tools/sweep-selftests.py, tools/affected.py, CHANGELOG.md and docs/research/pipeline-cost-levers.md only reference the test file's path, which is unchanged. NOT EDITED, OUTSIDE MY FILES, AND THEY NEED A FOLLOW-UP: plugins/audit/reference/verbs-in-full.md (~line 266 and the paragraph at ~1269, '`--gate-clear` is how a task reaches the EMPTY gate') now omits that a tdd/regression task refuses it. tasks.title: A task that deletes, renames or changes a file other files read cannot be dispatched until each such dependant is declared or waived with a reason, and scope can add files without restating the held list
tasks.description: Register F792 (verified open 2026-10-31 at ad838231; recurred twice in P151 and three times in P143 as undeclared edits). The brief already lists "Who depends on this" (audit-lookup.dependant_lines) but only asks the executor to answer each dependant, and nothing grades it. Do: from the same dependants data, list at dispatch every tracked file that reads a declared file (by path, by import, or by text anchor, e.g. tools/prove-gates.py rows anchored on ci.yml and gate-parity.py text) that the task does not declare, and refuse dispatch until each is declared or waived with a recorded reason. Also let scope take an incremental +a,b spelling. Keep the refusal precise: a dependant that cannot be affected by the declared change shape must not be demanded (measure the false-positive rate over the last phases P143 and P151 and report it).
